title: Misunderstanding the boss's 'get off' at the Nest
summary: Not knowing New York lingo, Bigard thought 'get off' meant leave the stand and began packing his horn; the boss meant he should take a chorus, and the band teased him.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: And so that way -- and the funny part, one night I didn't understand the New York lingo with musicians at that time. So the boss came around -- he used to walk on the floors. He looked at me and said, "C'mon, boy, get off, get off, get off." So I thought he said get off the stand and I started packing my horn. He came back and said, "Where the hell you going?" I said, "I'm going home. You said get off." He says, "You dummy. I meant for you to take a chorus." He wanted me to jam a chorus. And everybody in the band started laughing. They didn't know what was happening, and after he told them, boy, they used to kid the devil out of me.
